sentences.text: Revenue compounded 24.2% a year, from $1.70 billion in FY2016 [F196][F1] to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F10].
Operating margin rose from 0.6% in FY2016 [F26] to 34.8% in FY2025 [F35], against a window median of 31.8% [D663].
Net income of $2.10 billion in FY2018 [F38] was lifted by a one-time $1.56 billion tax benefit from releasing the valuation allowance [P52].
The FY2024 operating loss of $233 million [F24] reflected $4.6 billion of acquired R&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine [P11].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO rose to 85.9% of FY2025 revenue [D529], from 62.3% in FY2020 [D516].
Its growth slowed to 0.7% in FY2025 [D530] from 14.5% in FY2024 [D527], contributing +0.7pp [D531].
ALYFTREK added +7.6pp of FY2025 growth [D590] from $838 million of sales [S69], after no sales in FY2024 [S68][P9].
Over the window, operating income compounded 95.6% a year [F197] against 24.2% for revenue [F196], so profit grew faster than sales.
Growth now rests on one product family, so its FY2025 slowdown matters more than any single new contributor.
Operating margin of 34.8% [F35] is above its 31.8% window median [D663] and below the FY2022 high of 48.2% [D662].
The FY2025 margin gain of 36.9pp [D452] sits mostly in the residual other-lines category at +37.7pp [D468], which the cited filings do not explain.
SG&A rose to 14.6% of revenue [D427] after 19.7% growth [D456], and the FY2024 filing expected further increases in 2025 [P6].
FY2024 tax of $784 million [X114] on $249 million of pre-tax income [X104] gave a 315.5% effective rate [D390], attributed to non-deductible Alpine AIPR&D [P5].
Operating cash flow of $3.63 billion [F85] was 0.92x net income [D434], and free cash flow was 0.81x [D435] against a window median of 1.07x [D675].
The filing attributes the $3.6 billion of operating cash flow mainly to $4.2 billion of operating income [F85][F25][P1].
Receivables grew 27.6% [D461] against 8.9% revenue growth [D446], and no passage in the pack explains the gap.
Capex of $438 million [F95] was 2.09x D&A [D436] and rose 47.0% [D447]; the pack holds no passage on the programme behind it.
Net cash of $12.3 billion [D439] is 102.7% of revenue [D440], ranking at the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers [D691], whose median is -50.7% [D692].
Cash and investments fell 18.2% in FY2024 [D416], mainly because of the Alpine payment and share repurchases [P10].
Buybacks and dividends of $2.02 billion [D441] took 63.2% of free cash flow [D442], leaving diluted shares unchanged at 258.0 million [X137][D459].
[R1] Days inventory outstanding rose to 373 days in FY2025 [D444] from 287 [D397], with inventory up 39.9% [D462]; no passage in the pack explains the build.
Days sales outstanding reached 62 [D443], above FY2022's 59 days [D297], as receivables grew 27.6% [D461] against 8.9% revenue growth [D446].
The FY2025 effective tax rate of 14.9% [D433] looks normal, so the [R2] candidate reflects the FY2024 distortion [D390] and is benign.
Operating margin should hold at or above its 31.8% window median [D663]; a fall below it would reverse the FY2025 recovery from 34.8% [F35], checked in the FY2026 10-K.
Days inventory outstanding should fall back toward 287 days [D397] from 373 days [D444]; a further rise would confirm [R1] in the FY2026 10-K.
Revenue growth should stay at or above the FY2025 rate of 8.9% [D446]; a fall below it, with TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth at 0.7% [D530], would confirm the slowdown in the FY2026 10-K.
